feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with strategy/operations leadership. Writing is polished overall, but the document is slightly repetitive and dense, with some style inconsistencies and a few grammar/punctuation issues that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions at one organization strongly support leadership growth and domain expertise.  
- Good impact signals: 10,000+ page migration, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers, and named tools/platforms add substance.  
- Strong positioning: summary and skills sections consistently reinforce digital strategy, governance, content operations, and technical fluency.

1. Top improvements  
- Tighten repetition and structure: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to reduce redundancy and free space for more quantified outcomes.  
- Add more results-focused bullets: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than outcomes; include measurable improvements in engagement, efficiency, adoption, or campaign performance.  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: use “12 years of experience” (not “12 years experience”); add serial commas consistently (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”); standardize hyphenation (“cross-channel” vs “Multi-channel”), capitalization, and bullet punctuation. No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be sharper with more specificity, a more current emphasis on strategy/platform transformation, and less overlap with the skills sections.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten the opening and fix grammar: use “12+ years of experience.”
- Lead with current senior-level value: digital strategy, platform modernization, governance, and cross-functional leadership.
- Add one or two concrete context cues from recent roles (e.g., mission-driven/member organizations, enterprise web ecosystems, advocacy communications).
- Reduce broad channel lists since web, email, social, and multimedia already appear throughout the CV.

Possible rewrite:
Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience shaping web, content, email, social, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, platform modernization, digital governance, and workflow design that enables complex teams to communicate effectively at scale. Strong background in advocacy and stakeholder communications, translating technical and policy issues into clear, accessible content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” repeats detail already covered extensively in Work Experience and skills sections.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. It would be more effective if tightened to emphasize strategic scope and distinctive strengths rather than broad, repeated phrases.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms like “Multi-channel communication” with stronger, CV-aligned phrasing such as “Cross-channel communications leadership.”
- Reduce overlap by focusing on higher-value capabilities: Digital strategy & platform modernization • Editorial systems & governance • Web/CMS administration • Analytics & performance reporting • Workflow architecture • Advocacy communications • Multimedia & live event production
- Standardize style: use either “and” or “&” consistently; “cross-department” is clearer than “cross department.”
- Consider separating “Stakeholder coordination” from competencies if it already appears under Soft Skills.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital strategy,” “advocacy communication,” and “stakeholder/cross-department coordination” are already prominent in the header and other skills sections.
- “Workflow design” and “systems architecture” may feel repetitive unless differentiated.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and NACo entries. Tighten it around 3–4 high-impact contributions and add outcomes, scale, or scope wherever possible.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper lead: “Embedded strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading web modernization, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise,” “deliver”) with ownership language: “Built,” “Led,” “Designed,” “Established,” “Improved.”
- Consolidate into impact-focused bullets, e.g.:
- Led Drupal-based campaign and storytelling builds, including microsites, modular content components, and member-facing resource toolkits.
- Built communications workflows, analytics, and governance practices to improve cross-channel coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.
- Directed an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows, and user discovery experience.
- Add metrics if available: number of sites/pages, users, publishers, campaign launches, time saved, engagement lift, or search success improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” repeats NACo and Core Competencies; keep only if tied to a distinct result.
- Drupal microsite and AI search also appear in Recent Projects/footer—avoid repeating the same phrasing.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics; it should be tightened to foreground enterprise outcomes and distinguish this director role from the earlier NACo positions. Emphasize transformation, team/operating ownership, and measurable business impact over channel descriptions.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget, leading enterprise platform modernization and multi-channel communications operations.”
- Rewrite bullets to lead with outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable impact where possible: email engagement growth, social growth, reporting efficiency, production cost/time savings from the studio, governance adoption, or reduced publishing bottlenecks.
- Combine tools into one impact-focused bullet: “Built analytics stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery to improve executive reporting and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise ownership and transformation.
- Video/studio language may duplicate older multimedia bullets unless framed as building new in-house capability at leadership level.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to what you owned at this level: executional leadership, editorial operations, and channel growth.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a tighter scope statement: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial delivery and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Replace “helping” language with direct ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Add outcomes if available: newsletter open/click rates, video views, publishing volume, campaign response, or turnaround improvements.
- Combine the last two bullets into one sharper line: “Built cross-team editorial planning and standardized publishing workflows, improving coordination, consistency and delivery speed.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with both the earlier role and Recent Projects; keep it here only if you can show expansion or measurable growth.
- Avoid repeating broad channel oversight already covered more strategically in the Director role.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline skills item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should be tighter, more distinctive, and framed around leadership scope rather than repeating generic capability labels.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad nouns with sharper, executive-level phrasing:  
- Enterprise digital strategy & transformation  
- Editorial governance & content operations  
- Cross-channel communications leadership  
- Public-sector, membership & advocacy messaging  
- Audience strategy, content planning & storytelling
- Consider reducing to 4 lines to improve scanability and avoid sounding repetitive.
- Use parallel structure throughout; currently “messaging” and “planning” feel less senior than “strategy” and “leadership.”
- If space allows elsewhere, reserve “audience-focused” language for experience bullets where outcomes can be shown.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” duplicate both the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” also overlaps with recent NACo and consulting experience; keep this skills block high-level and non-repetitive.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes over exhaustive tool naming.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Drupal and enterprise CMS delivery” instead of listing multiple platforms flatly.
- Cut lower-priority/older-feeling items here that are already covered elsewhere, and keep the most marketable themes tied to recent work.
- Suggested rewrite: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Consider dropping jQuery from this topline section unless it is required for target roles; it weakens the senior/modern positioning.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT”; avoid repeating WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages unless they are important for the target job.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies and the header summary; keep wording consistent but not repetitive.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for the recent NACo and consulting work, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + outcome language, e.g. “Analytics infrastructure, KPI design and executive reporting.”
- Tighten and group related items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity” instead of separate bullets if space is tight.
- Replace “SEO and performance analysis” with more strategic phrasing like “SEO, UX and content performance analysis.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics infrastructure (GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity) • KPI design and dashboarding • Executive/leadership reporting • SEO, UX and content performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Avoid repeating the exact same tool list in both Topline Skills and Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills more strategic.

- Replace generic phrasing with outcome-oriented capability language, e.g. “Broadcast-quality video production” instead of “Video production and editing.”

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either be tightened to emphasize strongest/recent CMS platforms or add light qualifiers that reflect actual depth.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize by relevance/recency: **Drupal (enterprise, Drupal 10)** • **WordPress** • **SharePoint** • **Power Pages** • GitHub Pages
- If space allows, add level cues instead of just names: **Drupal (primary enterprise CMS)** • **WordPress (site builds/content ops)** • **SharePoint/Power Pages (Microsoft ecosystem)** • GitHub Pages
- Consider renaming the heading to **CMS & Web Publishing Platforms** for clearer distinction from coding/tools.
- Keep GitHub Pages only if it supports a real project or portfolio use case; otherwise cut it to keep the list stronger.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; avoid repeating the exact same platform list in both places.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles, so this section should complement that evidence, not restate it.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and modern tools most aligned with recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from broad coding languages to applied execution: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Group tools by function for clarity: “Integrations & deployment: API integrations, GitHub Actions, Cloudflare Workers”
- Keep only tools you actively used in recent roles/projects; if possible, swap in stronger specifics like “custom Drupal theming,” “component-based front-end builds,” or “tag implementation via Google Tag Manager”
- Consider revised line: “Front-end implementation (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Workflow automation” is covered elsewhere, so avoid implying GitHub Actions belongs in that broader category unless supported by project examples.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. Since “workflow automation” already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills, this item should be tighter and more systems-oriented.

Suggested edit
- Reframe by function, not just brand names: “Workflow automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Teams”
- Put the strongest, most relevant tools first based on recent work: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana.
- Consider trimming lower-value/general collaboration tools if space is tight; Slack and Teams are widely assumed unless central to your systems work.
- If possible, add scope in a nearby role bullet instead of here, e.g., “Built cross-team workflow systems in Airtable/Power Automate to streamline publishing and reporting.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp overlap as project-management tools; listing all four may feel redundant unless each was materially used.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this item is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses a chance to signal scale or use case. Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent NACo roles, keep this concise and platform-focused rather than repeating newsletter management.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten platform naming for readability: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add one qualifier to show depth without duplicating experience bullets: **campaign automation, newsletter operations, audience segmentation**
- Optional stronger version: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • Email automation • Audience segmentation**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding claims like “managed newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here; that impact is already covered in Work Experience.
- If Dynamics 365 was only lightly used, consider dropping it or moving it later in the list to avoid overstating proficiency.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete outputs if you can add metrics.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe around early-career buildout: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital media function…”
- Emphasize distinct contributions: website refresh support, livestream/video production, and workflow setup across web/email/social/multimedia.
- Tighten phrasing and remove filler like “high-impact” and “day-to-day”; replace with specifics and scale.
- Example rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital media team. Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and helped formalize cross-channel workflows across web, email, social and multimedia. Provided informal supervision and production guidance to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; if kept here, frame it as launching or initially producing the series.
- Avoid repeating team-building/governance language already used more strongly in the Director role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Emphasize coordination + launch impact, and trim broad phrases like “supporting organizational programs and policy work.”

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the standout achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives for county-focused programs and policy teams, while supporting early digital content production.”
- Make the podcast launch the second sentence and tighten verbs: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- If possible, add scope or output: number of projects supported, episodes produced, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders coordinated.
- Remove filler like “contributed to multimedia materials” unless you can specify formats or outcomes.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later Digital Media Manager/Producer and Associate Communications Director entries.
- Avoid overstating digital leadership here; later NACo roles already show progression into that space.
